output.summary: An evergreen tree or large shrub native to Japan, Korea, northeastern China and extreme southeastern Russia, Japanese yew has flat, dark green leaves. Its single seed sits partly inside bright red, berry-like flesh. Every part except that flesh is toxic, with seeds containing the highest toxin concentrations.
output.edibilityNote: All parts except the red aril are toxic; ingested leaves or seeds require urgent medical advice, and seeds contain the most toxin.
